skills/toil/sde.md

Projects, countermeasures (tasks), threats and users on SD Elements, through its REST API v2 (/api/v2/...). Every command reads; none changes anything. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest SD Elements version toil supports hasn’t been established. toil calls /api/v2/ with an API token sent as Authorization: Token. server-info reports the version but needs a super-user, so toil makes no version check. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

An SD Elements API token: in SD Elements, your user menu → API Tokens. toil sends it as Authorization: Token <token>. There is no username, password or browser login, and no CI fallback variable.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
connectionStringTOIL_SDE_CONNECTION_STRINGyesAPI token and server host in one value, <token>@<host>
projectTOIL_SDE_PROJECTnoDefault project ID for project, tasks, task and threats

The connection string holds both the token and the host: abc12345@sde.imagile.dev, or abc12345@imagile.sdelements.com for a hosted tenant. toil splits it at the first @, and the host gets https:// unless it already has a scheme (abc12345@https://sde.imagile.dev/sde keeps a context path). A value with no @, or with @ first, sets nothing, and commands fail with NOT_CONFIGURED. An env value beats the config file.

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_SDE_CONNECTION_STRING=<your API token>@sde.imagile.dev

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with project usually set once under defaults.sde:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "corp-sde": { "area": "sde" }
  },
  "defaults": { "sde": { "connection": "corp-sde", "project": "42" } }
}

The connection string holds the token, so it never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add corp-sde --area sde (or toil connections login corp-sde for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_SDE_CONNECTION_STRING.

Commands

The project ID comes from --project <id> (--id <id> on project), else the connection’s project (usually defaults.sde.project). With neither, the command fails with “No project specified”; anything but a positive whole number fails with “Invalid project ID”. Both happen before any request.

  • server-info: Get server version and platform info. SD Elements answers only a super-user.
  • whoami: Get current authenticated user (/api/v2/users/me/).
  • users: List users (--email, --first-name, --last-name, --active true|false).
  • projects: List projects (--name, --search, --active true|false|all, --ordering, --expand, --include).
  • project: Get a single project by ID (--id, --expand, --include).
  • tasks: List countermeasures for a project (--phase, --priority, --status, --assigned-to, --source, --verification, --tag, --accepted, --relevant, --expand, --include).
  • task: Get a single countermeasure (--task, required). Pass the composite ID from tasks (id, such as 42-T21); the value goes into the path as given, so the bare task_id (T21) asks for a different path and SD Elements likely answers NOT_FOUND.
  • threats: List threats for a project (--severity, --search, --ordering, --capec-id, --component-id).

Only --active is checked; every other filter goes to the server as given.

users, projects, tasks and threats page with --page (default 1) and --page-size (default 100), each a positive whole number; data is then SD Elements’ own page, { count, next, previous, results }, with next and previous passed through as the server’s URLs. --all ignores both and fetches every page, 100 at a time, until count is reached or a page comes back empty; data is then one bare list of results. --all also stops with an error after 1,000 pages (100,000 items), and like every command it’s subject to toil’s time limit (TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS, 120 s by default).

toil sde whoami
toil sde projects --active true --all
toil sde tasks --project 42 --phase development --page-size 50
toil sde task --project 42 --task 42-T21 --expand status,phase

Settings at a glance

  • connectionString secret

    API token and server host in one value, <token>@<host>, e.g. abc12345@sde.imagile.dev or abc12345@imagile.sdelements.com

    TOIL_SDE_CONNECTION_STRING

  • project

    Default project ID for project, tasks, task and threats

    TOIL_SDE_PROJECT

Commands at a glance

  • toil sdeserver-info

    Get server version and platform info (requires super-user)

    MCP sde_server_info

  • toil sdewhoami

    Get current authenticated user

    MCP sde_whoami

  • toil sdeusers

    List users

    MCP sde_users--email <email>--first-name <name>--last-name <name>--active <bool>--page <n>--page-size <n>--all

  • toil sdeprojects

    List projects

    MCP sde_projects--name <name>--search <text>--active <val>--ordering <field>--expand <fields>--include <fields>--page <n>--page-size <n>--all

  • toil sdeproject

    Get a single project by ID

    MCP sde_project--expand <fields>--include <fields>--id <id>

  • toil sdetasks

    List countermeasures for a project

    MCP sde_tasks--phase <slug>--priority <n>--status <id>--assigned-to <email>--source <val>--verification <val>--tag <name>--accepted <bool>--relevant <bool>--expand <fields>--include <fields>--page <n>--page-size <n>--all--project <id>

  • toil sdetask

    Get a single countermeasure

    MCP sde_task--task <id>--expand <fields>--include <fields>--project <id>

  • toil sdethreats

    List threats for a project

    MCP sde_threats--severity <n>--search <text>--ordering <field>--capec-id <id>--component-id <id>--page <n>--page-size <n>--all--project <id>
